Corseting is great for really understanding proper posture. You can't slouch and you really feel which muscles you should be using to stand up straight.

To that end, there are stretches and exercises that can help.

Poor posture is typically expressed with ‘tech neck.’ YouTube has some great examples of how to stand straighter, but I recommend laying on ones back at the edge of an ottoman or other furniture and letting the head roll back, stretching the cervical spinal (neck spine in layman’s terms) joints that are typically frozen. Once moved, tilt your head down from the top while maintaining that rolled back posture.

It will be hard to breathe at first, and deeply uncomfortable and even difficult to maintain as the muscles in your neck are not used to actually holding your head up. That will change in time. I also recommend rolling back your shoulders- chest out, chin up, to help maintain that posture. Again, you may feel a strain from your sternum through the tops and insides of your shoulders as those muscles have been drawn artificially tight by the shame and slouch we have been indoctrinated to feel. Stretching them to their natural state may feel uneasy at first.

But it will soon give you what others will describe as ‘a presence,’ and help others to take notice of you.

Proper posture will also prevent or alleviate back and neck injuries, which can otherwise cause pain locally or elsewhere, like in other joints or as headaches.
